title: A Tsetlin Machine-driven Intrusion Detection System for Next-Generation IoMT Security
new_feature: Vanilla TM intrusion detection system for IoMT network traffic on CICIoMT-2024 in binary (Bluetooth), 6-class (MQTT+Wi-Fi) and 7-class (all protocols) settings, with class-vote and clause-activation-heatmap explanations.

datasets.split_as_reported: official per-protocol train/test files; missing values and duplicates removed (train 21,750 benign / 65,549 DoS; test 6,533 / 23,979 per Fig. 3); SMOTE on training only; five-fold CV also mentioned
datasets.notes: Benign vs DoS. Raw: train 121,590 / test 31,704 (Table II). Dataset from Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (40 IoMT devices).
datasets.booleanization: standardisation then KBinsDiscretizer (5 quantile bins, one-hot dense) for TM only

datasets.split_as_reported: official train/test files after cleaning (counts from Fig. 8); SMOTE on training for TM, class weights for ML models
datasets.notes: Benign, DoS, DDoS, Recon, MQTT, Spoofing. Raw: train 6,987,390 / test 2,175,604 (Table II).
datasets.booleanization: standardisation then KBinsDiscretizer (5 quantile bins, one-hot dense) for TM only

datasets.input_shape_or_features: 11 features common to Bluetooth and MQTT/Wi-Fi
datasets.split_as_reported: official train/test files after cleaning (Fig. 14, per-class counts hard to attribute in extracted text); SMOTE for TM
datasets.booleanization: standardisation then KBinsDiscretizer (5 quantile bins, one-hot dense) for TM only

extraction_notes: Metrics in Tables IV/VI/VIII are given as fractions under '(in %)' headers; converted to percent with 1 decimal. Evaluation reported on official test files, though the paper also says five-fold CV is employed - which one produced the tables is ambiguous. Scenario 3 sample counts in Fig. 14 could not be reliably attributed to train/test per class, so sizes left null. Train/test sizes for scenarios 1-2 are sums of Fig. 3/Fig. 8 class counts.
